terms.text: 'Audit' means the systematic, independent and documented process for obtaining audit evidence and evaluating objectively to determine the extent to which the audit criteria are fulfilled.
'Audit criteria' means a set of requirements used as a reference against which audit evidence is compared.
'Audit evidence' means records, statements of fact or other information which are relevant to the audit criteria and verifiable.
'Audit finding' means an audit criteria not being met.
'Audit period' means the period of time to which the audit work relates and from which audit evidence is obtained.
'Audit subject' means the CII system that is to be audited.
'Adequacy of control' means whether the control in place is fit for the purpose.

'Compensating control' (also called an alternative control) means a control that may be considered when an entity cannot meet a requirement explicitly as stated, due to legitimate technical or documented business constraints, but has sufficiently mitigated the risk associated with the requirement through implementation of other controls. A compensating control must: (a) meet the intent and rigour of the original requirement; (b) provide a similar level of defence as the original requirement; and (c) be commensurate with the additional risk imposed by not adhering to the requirement.
'Effectiveness of control' means whether the control in place has the desired effect of mitigating the risk.
'Interim control' means a set of measures designed to reduce the risk temporarily while the recommended control is being implemented.
